Trap Space The small clam is often found buried, a wide 
expanse of tendrils spread outwards over a 10 ft. Square 
beneath the sand.
Countering The adhesive tendrils, when not covered in gains 
of sand, can be seen glistening in the light. Wisdom (Perception) 
Check: DC 10. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Nestled a few inches beneath the beach, the clam slowly 
spreads a network of clear tendrils throughout the sands, much 
like mycelia. These tendrils have a quick acting neurotoxin 
that numbs the flesh and tenses muscles tightly, causing the 
creatures to fall listly to the sand and slowly drown in the rising 
tide. Their decaying bodies nourishing the clam beds.
Senses None
Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, 
Frightened, Prone

Numbing Tendrils Trigger: When a creature steps within its 
Trap Space. Response - Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, the 
creature that triggered the Trap. Failure: The target has the 
Paralyzed condition, and can repeat the Saving Throw at the 
end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. 
The numbing lasts for 1 minute once out of the space and the 
creature can then move normally.
Trap Space The carnivorous plant grows on vertical surfaces, its 
primary stalk able to shift slightly to allow its wide peristome 
to catch falling creatures within a 5 ft. Sphere.
Trap Space The hydrozoan colony floats in the center of a 10 ft. 
Circle, its tendrils spreading out widely.
Trap Space The towering starfish moves at a slow measured 
pace. Passively stinging any creatures that enter a space within 
a 5 ft. Circle.
Countering The mawgraw is not a plant attempting to hide 
and can be found along coastal cliffs, hoping to capture curious 
birds or falling terrestrial animals.
Countering Like a small island, the colony is easily seen above 
the waves. Below the water, the translucent stinging tendrils are 
difficult to perceive. Wisdom (Perception) check: DC 14. Success: The 
Natural Trap’s tendrils are identified.
Countering The torrum, with its obvious height, is easily 
spotted, so it is recommended to use ranged weaponry or 
weapons with Reach to cut it down.
With so much teeming life along the intertidal zone of 
Sol’Kesh’s coasts, flora and fauna cling to every niche they can. 
Along the sheer rocky cliffs, amongst the barnacles and clams, 
some plants have taken root. The mawgraw's slight ability to 
move its peristome opening to capture live pray allows it to 
thrive.
The havrenn is unlike any other creature and is more known for 
its symbiotic nature than its lethality. Comprised of a hydrozean 
colony of polyps in a bowl-shaped form with trailing paralytic 
tendrils, that then safeguards a unique species of sea-lichen. 
Together this life raft floats off shore, with the lichen soaking in 
the sun safely, while the many trailing tendrils protect it from sea-
bound herbivores. 
Capitalizing on the exposed coral of the Strands, starfish soon 
evolved to not only rise past the tide, but grow to large sizes 
to stave off the predation of birds. The torrum stands above 
most, as it slowly crawls over smaller mollusks to feast, tendrils 
infused with a mind altering neurotoxin along its back deter 
predators, compelling them to keep away from the beach.

Gulping Maw Trigger: When a Medium or smaller creature 
enters its Trap Space. Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 
14, the creature that triggered the Trap. Failure: The target is 
swallowed by the plant. A swallowed creature has the Blinded 
and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against attacks and 
other effects outside the plant, and takes 7 (2d6) Acid damage 
at the start of each of its turns. If the plant takes 2 damage or 
more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the creature 
breaks free and falls in a space within 5 ft. (in addition to any 
vertical space to the ground) of the plant and has the Prone 
condition. If the plant dies, any swallowed creature no longer 
has the Restrained condition and can escape from the plant 
using 5 ft. of movement, exiting Prone.
Trailing Searing Tentacles Trigger: When a creature enters its 
Trap Space below the water. Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: 
DC 16, the creature that triggered the Trap. Failure: 1d8 Poison 
damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute, taking 1 
Poison damage at the beginning of their turn, the target can repeat 
the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect 
on itself on a success.
Sea Bound Tendrils Trigger: When a Medium or smaller 
creature enters its Trap Space. Response - Constitution Saving 
Throw: DC 12, the creature that triggered the Trap. Failure: The 
creature has the Poisoned condition for 10 minutes and can 
repeat the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns. While 
poisoned, the creature is compelled to swim in the ocean, and 
must use their movement each turn to get closer to the water, 
by the most direct route. If restrained or blocked, they become 
agitated and take 2 (1d4) Psychic damage for each minute they 
are prevented from moving toward the sea.
